← All split-fleet examples

F1 continuous carry: fleets seeded by ranking, qualifying scores carry into the final total, Gold outranks Silver

ILCA 7 2022 — World Championship, Vallarta MEX · F1 · SI (reference-docs:events/ilca7-worlds-2022/SI.pdf) · results (reference-docs:events/ilca7-worlds-2022/results-sailwave.html)

2 qualifying fleets · → Gold/Silver · discards: 1 discard from race 4.
The Addendum-C classic, with the assignment computed rather than declared:
- Round 1 is SEEDED from the entry ranking — competitors are listed in seed
  order (s1 best), and the serpentine spreads ability across flights, so s1
  and s2 land in DIFFERENT flights (Yellow gets s1, s4, s5; Blue gets s2,
  s3, s6). This is the point of seeding — consecutive seeds never share a
  flight — and `expectedFleets` asserts it.
- The final split is derived from the qualifying ranking: Gold = the top
  block, Silver = the rest.

Real Vallarta was 2 flights (Gold 63 / Silver 63), 6 Q + 6 F races, DNC base
= largest flight + 1 = 64, "max one final-series discard" (SI 18.3.3),
champion J-B Bernaz (FRA) 51 net. Reduced here to 2 flights of 3 over
Q1-Q2 + F1-F2 so a scorer can verify every cell.

Teaching points: qualifying scores stay in the total (continuous carry),
and Gold outranks Silver regardless of points. `expected` verified against
the engine.
